question: What are the two main parts that make up any computer system?
explanation: Hardware refers to the physical machinery while software provides the coded instructions that make the hardware work. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h1)

question: What happens immediately after a nurse enters patient data into a computer?

options.B: The printer immediately prints a receipt
options.C: The data is processed by the system

explanation: Once input is received, the computer processes the information according to programmed instructions before storing or displaying it. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h1)

question: Which tool is a standard input device used to identify patients in the ward?
explanation: Barcode scanners read patient ID bands, feeding that data directly into the computer to confirm identity before medication administration. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h2)

question: How does a bedside vital signs monitor screen act as an output device?

options.A: It shows the patient pulse and blood pressure numbers visually
options.B: It reads the microchip inside the patient drug infusion bag
options.C: It allows the nurse to type in the patient admission number
options.D: It records the voice notes dictated by the attending doctor

explanation: Output devices take processed electronic data and present it in a human-readable format like text, numbers, or images on a screen. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h2)

question: What is the primary function of the CPU in a hospital computer?

options.A: Supplying backup electrical power during blackouts
options.B: Connecting the workstation to the internet network
options.C: Processing data and executing system instructions
options.D: Storing permanent backups of discharged patient files

explanation: The CPU acts as the central brain that handles calculations and runs all programs on the machine. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h3)

question: What happens to data stored in the RAM when the computer loses power?

options.A: It stays visible on the monitor screen
options.B: All data in RAM is completely lost
options.C: It moves to permanent read-only memory
options.D: The data is automatically saved to the printer

explanation: RAM is volatile memory, meaning it requires electrical power to retain information and wipes clean when power is interrupted. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h3)

question: Why are Solid State Drives preferred over traditional hard drives in mobile nursing laptops?

options.A: They have no moving parts and resist physical shock better
options.B: They are completely immune to computer virus infections
options.C: They do not require any electricity to save files
options.D: They can connect directly to the hospital water supply

explanation: SSDs use flash memory chips instead of spinning platters, making them much less likely to break when carried around busy hospital wards. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is the main difference between computer memory and storage?

options.A: Storage deletes files every midnight automatically
options.B: Storage only handles graphics while memory handles text input
options.C: Storage keeps data permanently even when powered off, unlike temporary memory
options.D: Memory is located outside the computer case while storage is inside

explanation: Memory is fast and temporary for current tasks, whereas storage holds large amounts of data securely over long periods. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is the main role of an operating system on a hospital computer?

options.A: Printing daily prescription lists for the pharmacy
options.B: Managing hardware and running other software programs
options.C: Connecting physical wires to the internet router
options.D: Diagnosing patient illnesses using artificial intelligence

explanation: The operating system acts as the foundation platform that coordinates physical components and lets applications run properly. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h5)

question: Which item is classified as application software rather than system software?

options.A: Device driver for the receipt printer

explanation: Application software is designed for end-user tasks like nursing documentation, whereas system software manages the machine itself. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h5)

question: What allows computers in different departments of a hospital to share patient data instantly?
explanation: Networks link separate workstations together, allowing seamless sharing of files and clinical records across the facility. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h6)

question: Why is network connectivity crucial for modern Electronic Health Records?

options.A: It prevents the computer hardware from overheating during heavy use
options.B: It automatically prints out paper charts at the end of every shift
options.C: It eliminates the need for passwords and security logins
options.D: It allows multiple departments to access live patient records at the same time

explanation: Networks enable real-time updates so nursing, pharmacy, and medical staff view synchronized patient information instantly. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h6)

question: What is the immediate action a nurse should take when leaving a computer terminal on the ward?
explanation: Locking the screen prevents unauthorized persons from viewing or modifying open patient records while the nurse is away. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h7)

question: Which of the following actions is NOT consistent with good computer data security in nursing?

options.A: Logging out of the electronic health record application after your shift
options.B: Reporting strange error pop-ups on your clinical terminal to IT staff
options.C: Writing your system password on a sticky note pasted on the monitor
options.D: Using privacy filters on screens facing public waiting areas

explanation: Sharing or displaying your password compromises account security and allows anyone to access records under your name. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h7)
